transcript.content: Hello, I'm glad you could make it in today. What brings you to the clinic?

Yeah, hi. Um... it's mostly just work stuff. I manage some health services, and... I don't know, if something takes real, sitting-down brain work—like the monthly reports, or trying to plan a multi-site event—I just... I hit a wall. 

I keep putting it off. Even when I know it matters. So... that's why I'm here.
How long have you been experiencing this difficulty with sitting down and doing this kind of work?

Um... almost two years. Like a year and eleven months, I guess. 

It really started after... well, a friend of mine passed away. I ended up taking on more of the league and outreach responsibilities after that, and... yeah. Just since then.
Over these past two years, have you been feeling persistently down, sad, or depressed most days?
No... not really. I mean, I was sad when it happened, obviously, but... I don't feel down all the time. Just... frustrated with work, mostly.
0.0 in the differential? Because the chief complaint is classic adult ADHD presentation: difficulty with sustained mental effort, putting off reports/planning, hitting a wall with sitting-down

Um... I'm sorry, I don't really know what you mean by that. The... differential? 

I'm not a doctor, I just manage the clinic schedules and staff. I just know I can't seem to get through my paperwork. Are you saying... that's what you think it is?
Sorry about that slip of medical jargon. To understand this better, did you have any similar struggles with focus, organization, or procrastination back when you were in school as a child?

Yeah... I suppose. Back in elementary school, my teachers would tell my parents I was bright, but... I guess I was always daydreaming. 

I'd lose worksheets a lot. My mom actually had to check my backpack every night, or... I just wouldn't remember to turn my homework in. So... yeah. I guess I did.
